name: ubersdr-desktop
description: UberSDR desktop client — the v2 web UI in an Electron shell with an instance chooser
author: MadPsy <madpsy@users.noreply.github.com>
//homepage: Required by the deb target, not decoration: dpkg's control file has a Homepage field and electron-builder refuses to build a package without something to put in it. The same two facts are why `author` gained an email — Maintainer is mandatory too, and the noreply form is deliverable-ish without publishing an inbox.
//desktopName: Read by Electron itself (app.setDesktopName) and by electron-builder, which writes it as StartupWMClass. They must agree or the desktop environment cannot match a running window to the .desktop entry, and the taskbar shows a generic icon. Electron's fallback is `${app.name}.desktop` = ubersdr-desktop.desktop, so that is the name to pin.
//macSigning: Gatekeeper refuses a downloaded app that is not both signed with a Developer ID Application certificate and notarised by Apple — signing alone is not enough since Catalina. electron-builder does all of it when the credentials are in the environment (CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD to sign, APPLE_API_KEY/APPLE_API_KEY_ID/APPLE_API_ISSUER to notarise); `hardenedRuntime` and `notarize` are already its defaults for mac, so there is nothing to switch on here. The entitlements the hardened runtime needs are in assets/entitlements.mac.plist and its .inherit. sibling — assets/ because that is this project's directories.buildResources, not the build/ that every tutorial names. build.sh reports which credentials it found before building, so an unsigned dmg is never a surprise.
//artifactName: The three per-target artifactName settings in build.appImage/nsis/dmg drop the version from the filenames, because the client's download links are constants. Every release hangs off the rolling `latest` tag, so the URL a running client opens (updates.js) is fixed — electron-builder's default ${productName}-${version}.${ext} would move the file on every bump and 404 every client already in the field. They are set per target rather than on build.win, because a Linux --package builds the Windows zip too and a name under build.win would apply to both, calling the zip 'Setup'. One template cannot serve two architectures, though, and Linux ships for two: the bare AppImage and .deb names here are x86_64's, and build.sh's build_linux passes -c.appImage.artifactName / -c.deb.artifactName for the arm64 run instead. Deliberately that way round — those bare URLs are what every installed client fetches to update, so they can never gain an -x64. (Out here with the note below because electron-builder validates the `build` object and rejects keys it does not know.)
//buildFiles: build.files is an allowlist, not a filter: anything not named there is left out of app.asar. A new top-level module therefore works under `npm start` and throws 'Cannot find module' only once packaged — so add it to build.files in the same commit that creates it. (This note lives out here because electron-builder validates the `build` object against a schema and rejects keys it does not know.)
//debDepends: build.deb.depends replaces electron-builder's default list rather than extending it, so the nine defaults are repeated verbatim and only the last two are ours. libasound2 and libgbm1 are hard DT_NEEDED entries of the Electron binary that nothing else in the closure pulls in — without them a minimal install fails at exec with a loader error, and libasound in particular is the only backend Chromium's Web MIDI has on Linux. Everything else the binary needs arrives transitively (libcups2, the X libs and libxkbcommon0 via libgtk-3-0, libdbus-1-3 via libatspi2.0-0, libnspr4 via libnss3). libasound2 is correct on Ubuntu 24.04 too, where libasound2t64 Provides it. libpulse0 is only dlopened — absent, Chromium falls back to raw ALSA and the output-device list gets much less useful — so it belongs in recommends, next to the speech-dispatcher pair that libspeechd.so.2 needs. (Note out here because electron-builder validates the `build` object and rejects keys it does not know.)
//protocols: ubersdr://connect?uuid=… — see deeplink.js. This entry is what makes the association exist on two of the three platforms: electron-builder writes CFBundleURLTypes into the macOS Info.plist and MimeType=x-scheme-handler/ubersdr into the Linux .desktop entry (whose Exec already ends in %U, so the URL reaches argv). It writes nothing for NSIS — on Windows the registration is entirely app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient at startup, which is called on every platform anyway.

extendInfo.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: UberSDR asks for the microphone only so macOS will reveal the names of your audio output devices. Nothing is recorded and nothing is sent anywhere.
